title: Development and internal validation of a nomogram for early prediction of deep vein thrombosis after liver transplantation: an exploratory machine-learning comparison.
summary: A 131-recipient retrospective transplant cohort compared ML algorithms with a parsimonious logistic nomogram for early postoperative DVT; the principal model was logistic regression, and the ML comparison was exploratory.
ai_technology: Machine-learning algorithms were compared with a parsimonious logistic-regression nomogram for early postoperative DVT prediction after liver transplantation; the principal approach was logistic regression.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: The comparison is exploratory within a retrospective 131-recipient cohort; the study does not establish benefit from model-guided prevention.
evidence.unknown: The 131-recipient study is retrospective and internally validated; the authors identify logistic regression as the main model, with ML comparisons exploratory and no external clinical validation.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning algorithms were compared with a parsimonious logistic-regression nomogram for early postoperative DVT prediction after liver transplantation; the principal approach was logistic regression.
